To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the clinical staging of HIV infection in children is a good surrogate for the CD4 count in the absence of HIV viral load testing; (2) the clinical staging system is a good surrogate in children of all ages, and (3) clinical staging is as effective in children as in adults.
the clinical staging system of the WHO (World Health Organization) is a valid tool for assessing the severity of HIV infection in infants and children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of HIV infection in children.
the development and application of new techniques for the study of the structure and dynamics of complex systems.
a number of aspects of HIV infection and AIDS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the clinical staging of HIV infection is not a good surrogate for CD4 cell count in HIV-inflicted children.
the CD4 count is the gold standard for assessing the immunological status of HIV-infected patients, and it is recommended for use in clinical practice.
the clinical staging of HIV infection is a good surrogate for CD4 cell count in HIV-inflicted children and adolescents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the clinical stage of HIV disease is a good surrogate marker for the CD4 count, at least in the first few years after infection.
the CD4 count has been the gold standard for monitoring HIV infection and for guiding clinical decisions in children.
clinical staging of HIV infection is a surrogate for CD 4 count in children.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to develop and validate a new clinical staging system for HIV-infected children that is based on a simple clinical assessment.
there is a need to improve access to HIV treatment in children, especially for those who are severely ill and have a CD4 count below 200.
the CD4 count, a marker of immune status, is a good predictor of mortality in HIV-infected adults.
